# Plan — Resolve all 8 open architecture decisions

## Context

`docs/architecture.md` §10 lists 8 PENDING decisions blocking implementation. Per `coding-principles.md` §7, no slice can start until they're resolved. This plan locks in concrete choices (informed by what the test suite actually requires) so `docs/architecture.md` can be updated once with a solid direction before any code is written.

The human has now answered every judgment call. Below are the **final** decisions; the next step is a single edit to `docs/architecture.md` that promotes them out of §10.

---

## Evidence gathered (test-suite & data inspection)

These constrain the decisions below — observed, not assumed.

- **Concurrency tests send PATCH _without_ a `version` field** (`concurrency.test.ts`: just `{ status: 'approved' }`). → Optimistic locking must be **server-internal**; the API contract does not expose a version.
- **Realtime client tries WebSocket first, falls back to SSE** (`tests/utils/events-client.ts`). Implementing **either alone** is sufficient.
- **Bulk poll**: 500ms interval, 30s timeout; 1000-row bulk must complete inside 30s; the only invariant on overlap is `completed + failed` covers all unique IDs and no corrupt status appears (`bulk-operations.test.ts`).
- **Performance p95 budgets** (`performance.test.ts`): list 100ms, filtered+sorted 200ms, search 300ms, stats 500ms, supplier perf 500ms, anomalies 1000ms.
- **Aggregation pinned values** (`tests/expected-values.json`): `total_orders=50000`, `total_revenue=2,318,108,880`, top-10 supplier IDs fixed. **Negative-quantity orders count toward totals.**
- **Data quirks**: 1 order has empty warehouse → NULL; category cycle exists at `cat_150↔151↔152`; ~37 country codes with non-ISO variants; `<script>` and `onmouseover` payloads in `notes`; `quantity` ranges include negatives down to −49.
- **Security**: SQL-injection in `status` filter must return 400; XSS in `notes` must round-trip without HTML escaping but with `Content-Type: application/json`; bulk >10,000 IDs → 400; negative `limit` → 400 or clamp.

---

## Final decisions (human-confirmed)

### 1. `src/` project structure — **Api + Importer (two .csproj)**

```
src/
├── OrderOps.slnx
├── OrderOps.Api/
│   ├── Program.cs
│   ├── Features/
│   │   ├── Orders/        (controller + service + repository + DTOs)
│   │   ├── Suppliers/
│   │   ├── Products/
│   │   ├── Anomalies/
│   │   ├── Bulk/          (controller + hosted worker + job repo)
│   │   └── Events/        (SSE hub)
│   ├── Infrastructure/    (Npgsql connection factory, Redis client, error middleware, cache invalidation)
│   └── schema.sql         (canonical schema, applied by Importer)
├── OrderOps.Importer/
│   ├── Program.cs         (console: applies schema, COPYs CSVs, idempotent)
│   └── OrderOps.Importer.csproj
└── OrderOps.Web/          (Vite + React + TS — see §7)
```

- Importer is run independently (`dotnet run --project src/OrderOps.Importer`) so reviewers see it as a deliberate isolated tool.
- SOLID boundaries come from feature folders inside Api, not extra csprojs.

### 2. Database schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  parent_id   varchar(16) NULL
    REFERENCES categories(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
    -- DEFERRABLE so the COPY load can insert rows in any order inside one tx;
    -- FK enforces no orphan parent_ids at commit time.
    -- Note: Postgres self-FKs do NOT prevent cycles; cat_150↔151↔152 will load.
    -- Cycles MUST be guarded in the recursive CTE used for category descent.
);

CREATE TABLE suppliers (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  email       text,
  rating      numeric(3,2),
  country     varchar(8),       -- non-ISO codes exist (DEN, GER, BRZ); store as-is
  active      boolean NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  category_id varchar(16) REFERENCES categories(id),
  sku         text,
  price       numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  supplier_id  varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(id),
  product_id   varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
  quantity     integer NOT NULL,            -- negatives allowed (returns)
  unit_price   numeric(12,2) NOT NULL,
  total_price  numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
  status       varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  priority     varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  warehouse    varchar(32) NULL,            -- empty CSV value → NULL
  notes        text,
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1   -- server-internal optimistic lock; never emitted in JSON
);

CREATE TABLE jobs (
  id          varchar(32) PRIMARY KEY,
  status      varchar(16) NOT NULL,         -- processing|completed|failed
  total       integer NOT NULL,
  completed   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  action      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  finished_at timestamptz NULL              -- written when worker mirrors final Redis state
);

-- Indexes (sized to performance budget, not speculative)
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status      ON orders(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_priority    ON orders(priority);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_supplier    ON orders(supplier_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_warehouse   ON orders(warehouse);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at  ON orders(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_price ON orders(total_price);
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_trgm ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
```

- **`version`** is internal — the API never accepts or returns it.
- **`parent_id` FK is on** (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED). Per human direction, prioritize correctness so malformed/orphan parent_ids are rejected. Cycles still exist in the seed data but are query-time concerns, handled in the recursive CTE.

### 3. CSV import — `OrderOps.Importer` console app, **truncate-and-COPY, idempotent**

- Apply `schema.sql` (uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), then within one transaction: `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED`, `TRUNCATE` in FK-safe order, `COPY` each CSV via Npgsql `BeginBinaryImport` (fastest path for 50k orders). Empty `warehouse` → NULL at parse time.
- Re-running is safe.
- Importer prints row counts on completion; exits non-zero if any count mismatches the CSV header parse.

### 4. Concurrency mechanism — **internal `version` column + `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for bulk**

- **Single PATCH:** repository runs `UPDATE orders SET status=@s, updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE id=@id AND version=@v RETURNING version`. If 0 rows → 409. Service reads `version` immediately before the UPDATE in the same connection.
- **Bulk worker:** for each batch chunk, `SELECT id, version FROM orders WHERE id = ANY(@ids) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — orders held by an overlapping job are silently skipped (counted as `completed` because the other job has already applied the same action). Then issue the conditional UPDATE. A transaction wraps the chunk so the row locks release on commit.
- No Redis lock on the write path.

### 5. Background job runtime — **In-process `Channel<BulkJob>` worker; state in Redis (primary) + Postgres mirror**

- Bulk endpoint enqueues onto `Channel.CreateUnbounded<BulkJob>()`; one `IHostedService` worker drains it. Easily meets <500ms response and 30s completion budgets.
- **Live state in Redis**: hash key `job:{id}` with fields `status, total, completed, failed`. Worker uses `HINCRBY` per processed row → `GET /api/jobs/:id` reads from Redis only (microsecond latency).
- **Postgres mirror**: a `jobs` row is written when the job is enqueued and updated to its terminal state when the worker finishes (one final UPDATE). This gives durable audit/observability without doubling write traffic.
- If Redis goes down mid-job, the API can fall back to the Postgres row for status (degraded but correct for already-finished jobs).

### 6. Real-time transport — **SSE only, in-process pub/sub via `EventHub`**

- Tests' client tries WS first then SSE — SSE alone passes.
- Controller streams `text/event-stream` using `IAsyncEnumerable`.
- A singleton `EventHub` holds a list of subscriber `Channel<EventEnvelope>`s; PATCH handler and bulk worker `Publish()` events; controller filters per-subscriber by `?supplier_id=...`.
- No Redis pub/sub (single API instance).

### 7. Frontend — **Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + TanStack Query + Recharts** at `src/OrderOps.Web/`

- Vite for dev/build, Tailwind for layout speed, TanStack Query for server state + caching, Recharts for the analytics dashboard.
- No SSR, no router heaviness.

### 8. Anomaly severity rubric — **financial-impact tiered**

| Bucket | Trigger |
|---|---|
| **high** | Any of: `negative_quantity`, `price_mismatch`, `timestamp_anomaly`. **OR** ≥3 anomaly types matched. **OR** order belongs to a `risky_supplier`. |
| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |

- Will be documented in `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md` once §1.4 is implemented.

### Cross-cutting: Redis usage map (per human "lean on Redis for speed")

| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk job state (live counters) | `HSET job:{id} status total completed failed` | TTL 24h after terminal state |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/orders/stats` | `SET stats:global` (JSON) | `DEL` on every successful PATCH and on bulk-job completion |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/suppliers/:id/performance` | `SET perf:{supplier_id}` (JSON) | `DEL` on PATCH/bulk completion that touches an order with that supplier |
| (Optional later) Real-time pub/sub | not used in MVP | n/a |

The cache layer is a **post-MVP speed pass** — implemented after every endpoint is functionally correct. Correctness over performance.

---

## Critical files to be modified after approval (the actual edit this plan unlocks)

- `docs/architecture.md`:
  - Promote each PENDING item from §10 into the section it belongs to:
    - §3 (frontend toolchain — confirmed Vite stack)
    - §4 (repo layout — add OrderOps.Importer + OrderOps.Web; show feature folders inside Api)

## Context

---

## Evidence gathered (test-suite & data inspection)

These constrain the decisions below — observed, not assumed.

- **Concurrency tests send PATCH _without_ a `version` field** (`concurrency.test.ts`: just `{ status: 'approved' }`). → Optimistic locking must be **server-internal**; the API contract does not expose a version.
- **Realtime client tries WebSocket first, falls back to SSE** (`tests/utils/events-client.ts`). Implementing **either alone** is sufficient.
- **Bulk poll**: 500ms interval, 30s timeout; 1000-row bulk must complete inside 30s; the only invariant on overlap is `completed + failed` covers all unique IDs and no corrupt status appears (`bulk-operations.test.ts`).
- **Performance p95 budgets** (`performance.test.ts`): list 100ms, filtered+sorted 200ms, search 300ms, stats 500ms, supplier perf 500ms, anomalies 1000ms.
- **Aggregation pinned values** (`tests/expected-values.json`): `total_orders=50000`, `total_revenue=2,318,108,880`, top-10 supplier IDs fixed. **Negative-quantity orders count toward totals.**
- **Data quirks**: 1 order has empty warehouse → NULL; category cycle exists at `cat_150↔151↔152`; ~37 country codes with non-ISO variants; `<script>` and `onmouseover` payloads in `notes`; `quantity` ranges include negatives down to −49.
- **Security**: SQL-injection in `status` filter must return 400; XSS in `notes` must round-trip without HTML escaping but with `Content-Type: application/json`; bulk >10,000 IDs → 400; negative `limit` → 400 or clamp.

---

## Final decisions (human-confirmed)

### 1. `src/` project structure — **Api + Importer (two .csproj)**

```
src/
├── OrderOps.slnx
├── OrderOps.Api/
│   ├── Program.cs
│   ├── Features/
│   │   ├── Orders/        (controller + service + repository + DTOs)
│   │   ├── Suppliers/
│   │   ├── Products/
│   │   ├── Anomalies/
│   │   ├── Bulk/          (controller + hosted worker + job repo)
│   │   └── Events/        (SSE hub)
│   ├── Infrastructure/    (Npgsql connection factory, Redis client, error middleware, cache invalidation)
│   └── schema.sql         (canonical schema, applied by Importer)
├── OrderOps.Importer/
│   ├── Program.cs         (console: applies schema, COPYs CSVs, idempotent)
│   └── OrderOps.Importer.csproj
└── OrderOps.Web/          (Vite + React + TS — see §7)
```

- Importer is run independently (`dotnet run --project src/OrderOps.Importer`) so reviewers see it as a deliberate isolated tool.
- SOLID boundaries come from feature folders inside Api, not extra csprojs.

### 2. Database schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  parent_id   varchar(16) NULL
    REFERENCES categories(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
    -- DEFERRABLE so the COPY load can insert rows in any order inside one tx;
    -- FK enforces no orphan parent_ids at commit time.
    -- Note: Postgres self-FKs do NOT prevent cycles; cat_150↔151↔152 will load.
    -- Cycles MUST be guarded in the recursive CTE used for category descent.
);

CREATE TABLE suppliers (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  email       text,
  rating      numeric(3,2),
  country     varchar(8),       -- non-ISO codes exist (DEN, GER, BRZ); store as-is
  active      boolean NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  category_id varchar(16) REFERENCES categories(id),
  sku         text,
  price       numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  supplier_id  varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(id),
  product_id   varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
  quantity     integer NOT NULL,            -- negatives allowed (returns)
  unit_price   numeric(12,2) NOT NULL,
  total_price  numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
  status       varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  priority     varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  warehouse    varchar(32) NULL,            -- empty CSV value → NULL
  notes        text,
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1   -- server-internal optimistic lock; never emitted in JSON
);

CREATE TABLE jobs (
  id          varchar(32) PRIMARY KEY,
  status      varchar(16) NOT NULL,         -- processing|completed|failed
  total       integer NOT NULL,
  completed   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  action      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  finished_at timestamptz NULL              -- written when worker mirrors final Redis state
);

-- Indexes (sized to performance budget, not speculative)
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status      ON orders(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_priority    ON orders(priority);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_supplier    ON orders(supplier_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_warehouse   ON orders(warehouse);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at  ON orders(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_price ON orders(total_price);
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_trgm ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
```

- **`version`** is internal — the API never accepts or returns it.
- **`parent_id` FK is on** (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED). Per human direction, prioritize correctness so malformed/orphan parent_ids are rejected. Cycles still exist in the seed data but are query-time concerns, handled in the recursive CTE.

### 3. CSV import — `OrderOps.Importer` console app, **truncate-and-COPY, idempotent**

- Apply `schema.sql` (uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), then within one transaction: `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED`, `TRUNCATE` in FK-safe order, `COPY` each CSV via Npgsql `BeginBinaryImport` (fastest path for 50k orders). Empty `warehouse` → NULL at parse time.
- Re-running is safe.
- Importer prints row counts on completion; exits non-zero if any count mismatches the CSV header parse.

### 4. Concurrency mechanism — **internal `version` column + `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for bulk**

- **Single PATCH:** repository runs `UPDATE orders SET status=@s, updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE id=@id AND version=@v RETURNING version`. If 0 rows → 409. Service reads `version` immediately before the UPDATE in the same connection.
- **Bulk worker:** for each batch chunk, `SELECT id, version FROM orders WHERE id = ANY(@ids) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — orders held by an overlapping job are silently skipped (counted as `completed` because the other job has already applied the same action). Then issue the conditional UPDATE. A transaction wraps the chunk so the row locks release on commit.
- No Redis lock on the write path.

### 5. Background job runtime — **In-process `Channel<BulkJob>` worker; state in Redis (primary) + Postgres mirror**

- Bulk endpoint enqueues onto `Channel.CreateUnbounded<BulkJob>()`; one `IHostedService` worker drains it. Easily meets <500ms response and 30s completion budgets.
- **Live state in Redis**: hash key `job:{id}` with fields `status, total, completed, failed`. Worker uses `HINCRBY` per processed row → `GET /api/jobs/:id` reads from Redis only (microsecond latency).
- **Postgres mirror**: a `jobs` row is written when the job is enqueued and updated to its terminal state when the worker finishes (one final UPDATE). This gives durable audit/observability without doubling write traffic.
- If Redis goes down mid-job, the API can fall back to the Postgres row for status (degraded but correct for already-finished jobs).

### 6. Real-time transport — **SSE only, in-process pub/sub via `EventHub`**

- Tests' client tries WS first then SSE — SSE alone passes.
- Controller streams `text/event-stream` using `IAsyncEnumerable`.
- A singleton `EventHub` holds a list of subscriber `Channel<EventEnvelope>`s; PATCH handler and bulk worker `Publish()` events; controller filters per-subscriber by `?supplier_id=...`.
- No Redis pub/sub (single API instance).

### 7. Frontend — **Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + TanStack Query + Recharts** at `src/OrderOps.Web/`

- Vite for dev/build, Tailwind for layout speed, TanStack Query for server state + caching, Recharts for the analytics dashboard.
- No SSR, no router heaviness.

### 8. Anomaly severity rubric — **financial-impact tiered**

| Bucket | Trigger |
|---|---|
| **high** | Any of: `negative_quantity`, `price_mismatch`, `timestamp_anomaly`. **OR** ≥3 anomaly types matched. **OR** order belongs to a `risky_supplier`. |
| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |

- Will be documented in `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md` once §1.4 is implemented.

### Cross-cutting: Redis usage map (per human "lean on Redis for speed")

| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk job state (live counters) | `HSET job:{id} status total completed failed` | TTL 24h after terminal state |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/orders/stats` | `SET stats:global` (JSON) | `DEL` on every successful PATCH and on bulk-job completion |

| (Optional later) Real-time pub/sub | not used in MVP | n/a |

The cache layer is a **post-MVP speed pass** — implemented after every endpoint is functionally correct. Correctness over performance.

|---|---|

| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |

| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|

  priority     varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  warehouse    varchar(32) NULL,            -- empty CSV value → NULL
  notes        text,
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1   -- server-internal optimistic lock; never emitted in JSON
);

CREATE TABLE jobs (
  id          varchar(32) PRIMARY KEY,
  status      varchar(16) NOT NULL,         -- processing|completed|failed
  total       integer NOT NULL,
  completed   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  action      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  finished_at timestamptz NULL              -- written when worker mirrors final Redis state
);

-- Indexes (sized to performance budget, not speculative)
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status      ON orders(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_priority    ON orders(priority);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_supplier    ON orders(supplier_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_warehouse   ON orders(warehouse);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at  ON orders(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_price ON orders(total_price);
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_trgm ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
```

- **`version`** is internal — the API never accepts or returns it.
- **`parent_id` FK is on** (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED). Per human direction, prioritize correctness so malformed/orphan parent_ids are rejected. Cycles still exist in the seed data but are query-time concerns, handled in the recursive CTE.

### 3. CSV import — `OrderOps.Importer` console app, **truncate-and-COPY, idempotent**

- Apply `schema.sql` (uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), then within one transaction: `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED`, `TRUNCATE` in FK-safe order, `COPY` each CSV via Npgsql `BeginBinaryImport` (fastest path for 50k orders). Empty `warehouse` → NULL at parse time.
- Re-running is safe.
- Importer prints row counts on completion; exits non-zero if any count mismatches the CSV header parse.

### 4. Concurrency mechanism — **internal `version` column + `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for bulk**

- **Single PATCH:** repository runs `UPDATE orders SET status=@s, updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE id=@id AND version=@v RETURNING version`. If 0 rows → 409. Service reads `version` immediately before the UPDATE in the same connection.
- **Bulk worker:** for each batch chunk, `SELECT id, version FROM orders WHERE id = ANY(@ids) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — orders held by an overlapping job are silently skipped (counted as `completed` because the other job has already applied the same action). Then issue the conditional UPDATE. A transaction wraps the chunk so the row locks release on commit.
- No Redis lock on the write path.

### 5. Background job runtime — **In-process `Channel<BulkJob>` worker; state in Redis (primary) + Postgres mirror**

- Bulk endpoint enqueues onto `Channel.CreateUnbounded<BulkJob>()`; one `IHostedService` worker drains it. Easily meets <500ms response and 30s completion budgets.
- **Live state in Redis**: hash key `job:{id}` with fields `status, total, completed, failed`. Worker uses `HINCRBY` per processed row → `GET /api/jobs/:id` reads from Redis only (microsecond latency).
- **Postgres mirror**: a `jobs` row is written when the job is enqueued and updated to its terminal state when the worker finishes (one final UPDATE). This gives durable audit/observability without doubling write traffic.
- If Redis goes down mid-job, the API can fall back to the Postgres row for status (degraded but correct for already-finished jobs).

### 6. Real-time transport — **SSE only, in-process pub/sub via `EventHub`**

- Tests' client tries WS first then SSE — SSE alone passes.
- Controller streams `text/event-stream` using `IAsyncEnumerable`.
- A singleton `EventHub` holds a list of subscriber `Channel<EventEnvelope>`s; PATCH handler and bulk worker `Publish()` events; controller filters per-subscriber by `?supplier_id=...`.
- No Redis pub/sub (single API instance).

### 7. Frontend — **Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + TanStack Query + Recharts** at `src/OrderOps.Web/`

- Vite for dev/build, Tailwind for layout speed, TanStack Query for server state + caching, Recharts for the analytics dashboard.
- No SSR, no router heaviness.

### 8. Anomaly severity rubric — **financial-impact tiered**

| Bucket | Trigger |
|---|---|
| **high** | Any of: `negative_quantity`, `price_mismatch`, `timestamp_anomaly`. **OR** ≥3 anomaly types matched. **OR** order belongs to a `risky_supplier`. |
| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |

- Will be documented in `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md` once §1.4 is implemented.

### Cross-cutting: Redis usage map (per human "lean on Redis for speed")

| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk job state (live counters) | `HSET job:{id} status total completed failed` | TTL 24h after terminal state |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/orders/stats` | `SET stats:global` (JSON) | `DEL` on every successful PATCH and on bulk-job completion |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/suppliers/:id/performance` | `SET perf:{supplier_id}` (JSON) | `DEL` on PATCH/bulk completion that touches an order with that supplier |
| (Optional later) Real-time pub/sub | not used in MVP | n/a |

The cache layer is a **post-MVP speed pass** — implemented after every endpoint is functionally correct. Correctness over performance.

## 5. Data Model (CSV → Postgres)

The CSV columns are fixed; type choices below are confirmed against the actual data:

| Table | CSV columns | Notes / edge cases (from README §Tips + data inspection) |
|---|---|---|
| `orders` | `id, supplier_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, total_price, status, priority, created_at, updated_at, warehouse, notes` | ~2% have `total_price ≠ quantity*unit_price`; ~200 have `updated_at < created_at`; some `quantity < 0` (returns, down to −49); 1 row has empty `warehouse` → NULL; XSS payloads (`<script>…`, `onmouseover=…`) in `notes` |
| `suppliers` | `id, name, email, rating, country, active, created_at` | `active` is `true`/`false` text → boolean; ~37 country codes including non-ISO variants (DEN, GER, BRZ); duplicate name variations |
| `products` | `id, name, category_id, sku, price` | `price` = catalog/base price; used by `price_consistency` & `price_spike` rules |
| `categories` | `id, name, parent_id` | Hierarchical; `parent_id` empty for roots; **real cycle in seed at `cat_150↔151↔152`** — must guard the recursive descent (Postgres self-FKs do NOT prevent cycles) |

**Valid order statuses:** `pending, approved, rejected, shipped, delivered, cancelled`.

### 5.1 Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  parent_id   varchar(16) NULL
    REFERENCES categories(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
);

CREATE TABLE suppliers (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  email       text,
  rating      numeric(3,2),
  country     varchar(8),
  active      boolean NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  category_id varchar(16) REFERENCES categories(id),
  sku         text,
  price       numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  supplier_id  varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(id),
  product_id   varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
  quantity     integer NOT NULL,
  unit_price   numeric(12,2) NOT NULL,
  total_price  numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
  status       varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  priority     varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  warehouse    varchar(32) NULL,
  notes        text,
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1   -- server-internal optimistic lock; never in JSON
);

CREATE TABLE jobs (
  id          varchar(32) PRIMARY KEY,
  status      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  total       integer NOT NULL,
  completed   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  action      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  finished_at timestamptz NULL
);
```

- `version` is **internal**: never accepted on PATCH input, never emitted in responses. Used by the conditional UPDATE in §8.1.
- `parent_id` FK is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` — load order in COPY is unconstrained inside one tx; orphan parent_ids are rejected at commit. Cycles in the seed data still load (FKs don't prevent them) and must be guarded query-side.
- `jobs` row is the **mirror** of Redis live state — see §8.2.

### 5.2 Indexes

```sql
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status      ON orders(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_priority    ON orders(priority);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_supplier    ON orders(supplier_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_warehouse   ON orders(warehouse);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at  ON orders(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_price ON orders(total_price);
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_trgm ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
```

The trigram index on `products.name` exists because `?search=` is case-insensitive substring on the joined `product_name` — a btree wouldn't help; a `gin_trgm_ops` index does.

### 8.1 Concurrency — internal `version` + `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`

- **Single PATCH:** repository runs `UPDATE orders SET status=@s, updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE id=@id AND version=@v RETURNING version`. If 0 rows affected → `409`. The service reads the current `version` immediately before the UPDATE in the same connection (read-your-writes). The version is **never** part of the API contract — tests send no version, and responses don't expose it. The `concurrency.test.ts` PATCH-race test passes because two concurrent UPDATEs read `version=v` and only one wins the conditional UPDATE.
- **Bulk worker:** for each batch chunk, run `SELECT id, version FROM orders WHERE id = ANY(@ids) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` inside a transaction. Orders held by an overlapping job's transaction are silently skipped — they are then counted as `completed` because the other job has already applied the same action. This satisfies the "each order processed exactly once across overlapping batches" invariant. No Redis lock on the write path.

### 8.2 Background Jobs — in-process `Channel<BulkJob>` + Redis-primary state + Postgres mirror

- Bulk endpoint enqueues onto `Channel.CreateUnbounded<BulkJob>()`; one `IHostedService` worker drains it. Easily meets the <500ms response and 30s completion budgets (50ms enqueue, work happens off the request path).
- **Live state in Redis**: hash `job:{id}` with fields `status, total, completed, failed`. Worker uses `HINCRBY` per processed row. `GET /api/jobs/:id` reads from Redis only — microsecond latency, never hits Postgres on hot path.
- **Postgres `jobs` mirror**: a row is INSERTed when the job is enqueued and UPDATEd to its terminal state on completion. Durable audit/observability without doubling write traffic during the run.
- **Failure mode**: if Redis is unavailable mid-job, the API can fall back to the Postgres row for status (degraded but correct for already-finished jobs).

### 8.3 Real-time — SSE only, in-process `EventHub`

- SSE is sufficient: the test client (`tests/utils/events-client.ts`) tries WebSocket first (3s timeout) and falls back to SSE on failure, so SSE alone passes `realtime.test.ts`.
- Implementation: a controller streams `text/event-stream` using `IAsyncEnumerable<EventEnvelope>`.
- A singleton `EventHub` (DI-registered) holds a list of subscriber `Channel<EventEnvelope>`s. The PATCH handler and the bulk worker call `Publish()`. The controller filters by `?supplier_id=...` per subscriber.
- No Redis pub/sub (single API instance is the deployment shape).

### 8.4 CSV Import — `OrderOps.Importer` console, truncate-and-COPY, idempotent

- Run as `dotnet run --project src/OrderOps.Importer`.
- Steps inside one transaction:
  1. Apply `schema.sql` (uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` form so re-runs are no-ops).
  2. `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED;`
  3. `TRUNCATE orders, products, suppliers, categories RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;`
  4. `COPY` each CSV via Npgsql `BeginBinaryImport` — fastest path for 50k orders. Empty `warehouse` → `NULL` at parse time.
- Re-running is safe: tests can drop and reload state freely. Importer prints row counts on completion and exits non-zero if any count mismatches the CSV header parse.

### 8.6 Security
- Notes/text fields contain XSS payloads — store as-is; never echo through HTML; ensure JSON encoding is correct.
- SQL injection: Dapper parameterizes by default; never string-concatenate user input into SQL.
- Sort field whitelist: `sort=...` must be checked against an allow-list of column names, never substituted directly.

### 8.7 Redis usage map

Redis is leaned on for speed; the cache layer is a **post-MVP pass** — every endpoint must be functionally correct against Postgres first, then cached.

| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk job state (live counters) | `HSET job:{id} status total completed failed`, `HINCRBY` per row | `EXPIRE 86400` on terminal state |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/orders/stats` | `SET stats:global` (JSON), no TTL | `DEL stats:global` on every successful PATCH and on bulk-job completion |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/suppliers/:id/performance` | `SET perf:{supplier_id}` (JSON), no TTL | `DEL perf:{supplier_id}` on PATCH/bulk that touches an order with that supplier |
| Real-time pub/sub | not used in MVP (single-instance deployment) | n/a |

Invalidation is explicit, not TTL-based — staleness during the concurrency tests would be visible. Every write path that mutates an aggregate must `DEL` the affected cache keys; this is enforced by routing all writes through a single `OrdersWriteService` that calls the cache invalidator after a successful Postgres commit.

### 8.8 Anomaly severity rubric

Severity is computed deterministically from the matched rule set on a single order:

| Bucket | Trigger |
|---|---|
| **high** | Any of: `negative_quantity`, `price_mismatch`, `timestamp_anomaly`. **OR** ≥3 anomaly types matched. **OR** order belongs to a `risky_supplier`. |
| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |

Rationale: financial-integrity bugs (negative quantity, price mismatch, impossible timestamps) directly affect reported revenue and audit accuracy → **high**. Governance/cost concerns (using an inactive supplier, unusual price spike) are operational risks → **medium**. After-hours alone is informational → **low**. Multi-rule matches escalate one tier because correlated anomalies on a single order are stronger evidence of underlying data corruption.

The full rubric (with worked examples) lives in `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md`, written when §1.4 is implemented.

# Coding Principles

These rules are binding. They apply to every change made by the AI assistant. They take precedence over default model behavior. When two rules conflict, prefer the stricter one and surface the conflict to the human owner.

---

## 1. Clean and scalable code

- Naming carries meaning. Identifiers must read like intent, not abbreviation soup.
- Pure functions where possible. Side effects are isolated and named.
- No dead code, no unused parameters, no leftover scaffolding.
- Be deliberate about allocations on hot paths. Aggregations that touch 50k rows cannot afford casual `IEnumerable` materializations.
- Choose data structures for the access pattern, not for what's familiar.

## 2. Small files, small functions

- A function does one thing. If a function name needs "And", split it.
- Soft ceiling: ~30 lines per function, ~250 lines per file. Crossing it is allowed only with a clear reason.
- Controllers are thin. They parse input, call a service, format output. They do not contain business logic.
- Repositories own SQL. Services own business rules. Controllers own HTTP. No layer-skipping.
- Group by feature when possible (e.g. `Features/Orders/`, `Features/Suppliers/`) rather than by technical role only.

## 3. Comments

- Default: write no comments. The code names things; the names explain.
- Only justified comments:
  - A non-obvious WHY (a hidden constraint, a perf trick, a workaround for a bug or an edge case in the dataset).
  - A regulatory/spec quote when the code looks wrong without it (e.g. "test expects exactly 10 entries").
- When you do comment, keep it to one line where possible. No banner comments, no boilerplate XML doc on every property, no narration of what the next line does.

## 4. SOLID, always

- **S** — Single responsibility. A class has one reason to change. The `OrderService` does not also send emails.
- **O** — Open/closed. New behavior is added by extension, not by editing battle-tested code paths.
- **L** — Liskov. A subtype must be a drop-in for its base. No "throw NotImplementedException".
- **I** — Interface segregation. Many small role-interfaces, not one god interface. Consumers depend only on what they use.
- **D** — Dependency inversion. Services depend on abstractions registered in DI, not on concrete `new`-ed dependencies. Static `DateTime.UtcNow` and `Guid.NewGuid` are exceptions only when not on a tested business path.

No corner cuts. If a "quick fix" violates SOLID, surface it and ask before merging.

## 5. End-of-session checks

After each implementation increment, before handing back to the human, perform and report:

1. **Typecheck / build** — `dotnet build` (and `tsc --noEmit` for the frontend) must pass with zero errors and zero warnings introduced by the change.
2. **Code review (self)** — re-read the diff with these principles in hand. Flag anything that violates them.
3. **Implementation confidence** — one of `low | medium | high`, with one sentence justifying it.
4. **Risk assessment** — top 3 risks introduced by this change (correctness, performance, security, regression). If none, say so explicitly.
5. **Edge-case audit** — list edge cases considered, edge cases handled, edge cases knowingly deferred. The dataset is full of traps (negative quantities, null warehouses, circular categories, XSS in notes, timestamp anomalies, duplicate names, mismatched prices, inactive suppliers with orders) — every change touching that surface must be checked against the relevant traps.
6. **Human-check summary** — after every feature implementation or bug fix, provide a short bulleted list of the most important modifications that the human reviewer should manually eyeball before approving. Examples: "new SQL in `OrderRepository.GetById` — verify the JOIN cardinality"; "changed default `limit` from 50 to 20 in `OrdersController` — confirm intentional"; "added new index migration — verify it doesn't conflict with existing index names". Keep it tight: 2–5 bullets, each ≤1 line. The goal is to direct human attention to the parts of the diff that are easy to miss in a quick scan and would be costly to get wrong.

Format the report consistently so it's easy to skim. Example:

> **Build:** clean. **Confidence:** medium. **Risks:** (1) … (2) … (3) … **Edges considered:** …; **handled:** …; **deferred:** … **Docs:** updated `architecture.md` §6.1 and §9. **Human-check:** (1) new index on `orders.created_at` — verify name doesn't collide; (2) tightened error response for 404 — confirm shape matches `tests/basic-crud.test.ts:42`.

## 6. MVC for the backend

- ASP.NET Core controllers (not minimal APIs) for the request surface.
- Models = DTOs for the wire + domain entities for the database. Do not leak entities into HTTP responses; map explicitly.
- Views in this context = the JSON response shapes. Their structure is fixed by the README and tests — never deviate.
- Controllers stay thin. Services own business logic. Repositories own data access.

## 7. Small increments, human gate

This is the strongest rule. Do not bypass it.

- Work in the smallest meaningful slice. Prefer "implement GET /api/orders/:id" over "implement all CRUD".
- After each slice: stop, summarize, run end-of-session checks (§5), wait for the human to review and commit.
- **Never invent design decisions.** If a piece of information is missing — schema choice, library choice, response field, severity rubric, edge-case behavior — **ask**. Do not guess and do not "make a reasonable assumption" silently.
- It is better to ask one extra question than to ship code that has to be ripped out.
- If you discover during implementation that a previously-agreed approach won't work, stop and surface it; do not pivot unilaterally.

## 8. Documentation must stay current

The project's docs are part of the contract — out-of-date docs are worse than no docs because they actively mislead the next session.

After **every** conversation that produces a meaningful change (new code, new decision, new dependency, scope change, scrap-and-rewrite, anomaly rubric tweak, new edge case discovered, etc.), before handing back to the human:

- Update **`architecture.md`**:
  - Promote any **PENDING** decision that became a real decision (move it from §10 Open Decisions into the relevant section, with the chosen approach).
  - Append to **§9 Done So Far** as new milestones land.
  - Add new constraints, new endpoints, new edge cases, new packages, new files of note.
  - Remove or correct any statement that is no longer accurate.
- Update **`coding-principles.md`** when a new working agreement, ban, or check is introduced. If the human says "from now on, X" — that's a principles update, not a one-off note.
- Create or update other docs only when warranted. **All project docs live under `docs/`** — never write a new `.md` outside that folder (exception: `README.md` at the root, which is the assignment spec and is read-only).
  - `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (the deliverable for human reviewers) — written/maintained near submission.
  - `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md` (deliverable) — updated each time the anomaly rules or severity rubric change.
  - Any new cross-cutting doc needs a one-line entry in `docs/architecture.md` so it's discoverable.
- Never let docs and reality drift. If you cannot update the doc in the same increment, raise it as a follow-up task and surface it to the human.

The end-of-session report (§5) must include a **Docs:** line stating which docs were updated, or `Docs: none needed (no semantic change)` with one-sentence justification.

---

## How to apply during a session

1. Read `architecture.md` and this file at the start of every non-trivial session.
2. Before writing code: confirm scope of the increment with the human.
3. While writing code: check rules §1–§4 continuously, not just at the end.
4. Before handing back: run the §5 checklist (now including the **Docs:** line) and update docs per §8.
5. After human review and commit: ask what the next slice is. Do not start a new slice on your own.

# Plan — Resolve all 8 open architecture decisions

## Context

`docs/architecture.md` §10 lists 8 PENDING decisions blocking implementation. Per `coding-principles.md` §7, no slice can start until they're resolved. This plan locks in concrete choices (informed by what the test suite actually requires) so `docs/architecture.md` can be updated once with a solid direction before any code is written.

The human has now answered every judgment call. Below are the **final** decisions; the next step is a single edit to `docs/architecture.md` that promotes them out of §10.

---

## Evidence gathered (test-suite & data inspection)

These constrain the decisions below — observed, not assumed.

- **Concurrency tests send PATCH _without_ a `version` field** (`concurrency.test.ts`: just `{ status: 'approved' }`). → Optimistic locking must be **server-internal**; the API contract does not expose a version.
- **Realtime client tries WebSocket first, falls back to SSE** (`tests/utils/events-client.ts`). Implementing **either alone** is sufficient.
- **Bulk poll**: 500ms interval, 30s timeout; 1000-row bulk must complete inside 30s; the only invariant on overlap is `completed + failed` covers all unique IDs and no corrupt status appears (`bulk-operations.test.ts`).
- **Performance p95 budgets** (`performance.test.ts`): list 100ms, filtered+sorted 200ms, search 300ms, stats 500ms, supplier perf 500ms, anomalies 1000ms.
- **Aggregation pinned values** (`tests/expected-values.json`): `total_orders=50000`, `total_revenue=2,318,108,880`, top-10 supplier IDs fixed. **Negative-quantity orders count toward totals.**
- **Data quirks**: 1 order has empty warehouse → NULL; category cycle exists at `cat_150↔151↔152`; ~37 country codes with non-ISO variants; `<script>` and `onmouseover` payloads in `notes`; `quantity` ranges include negatives down to −49.
- **Security**: SQL-injection in `status` filter must return 400; XSS in `notes` must round-trip without HTML escaping but with `Content-Type: application/json`; bulk >10,000 IDs → 400; negative `limit` → 400 or clamp.

---

## Final decisions (human-confirmed)

### 1. `src/` project structure — **Api + Importer (two .csproj)**

```
src/
├── OrderOps.slnx
├── OrderOps.Api/
│   ├── Program.cs
│   ├── Features/
│   │   ├── Orders/        (controller + service + repository + DTOs)
│   │   ├── Suppliers/
│   │   ├── Products/
│   │   ├── Anomalies/
│   │   ├── Bulk/          (controller + hosted worker + job repo)
│   │   └── Events/        (SSE hub)
│   ├── Infrastructure/    (Npgsql connection factory, Redis client, error middleware, cache invalidation)
│   └── schema.sql         (canonical schema, applied by Importer)
├── OrderOps.Importer/
│   ├── Program.cs         (console: applies schema, COPYs CSVs, idempotent)
│   └── OrderOps.Importer.csproj
└── OrderOps.Web/          (Vite + React + TS — see §7)
```

- Importer is run independently (`dotnet run --project src/OrderOps.Importer`) so reviewers see it as a deliberate isolated tool.
- SOLID boundaries come from feature folders inside Api, not extra csprojs.

### 2. Database schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE categories (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  parent_id   varchar(16) NULL
    REFERENCES categories(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
    -- DEFERRABLE so the COPY load can insert rows in any order inside one tx;
    -- FK enforces no orphan parent_ids at commit time.
    -- Note: Postgres self-FKs do NOT prevent cycles; cat_150↔151↔152 will load.
    -- Cycles MUST be guarded in the recursive CTE used for category descent.
);

CREATE TABLE suppliers (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  email       text,
  rating      numeric(3,2),
  country     varchar(8),       -- non-ISO codes exist (DEN, GER, BRZ); store as-is
  active      boolean NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  category_id varchar(16) REFERENCES categories(id),
  sku         text,
  price       numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id           varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
  supplier_id  varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(id),
  product_id   varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
  quantity     integer NOT NULL,            -- negatives allowed (returns)
  unit_price   numeric(12,2) NOT NULL,
  total_price  numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
  status       varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  priority     varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
  warehouse    varchar(32) NULL,            -- empty CSV value → NULL
  notes        text,
  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1   -- server-internal optimistic lock; never emitted in JSON
);

CREATE TABLE jobs (
  id          varchar(32) PRIMARY KEY,
  status      varchar(16) NOT NULL,         -- processing|completed|failed
  total       integer NOT NULL,
  completed   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  failed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  action      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  finished_at timestamptz NULL              -- written when worker mirrors final Redis state
);

-- Indexes (sized to performance budget, not speculative)
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status      ON orders(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_priority    ON orders(priority);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_supplier    ON orders(supplier_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_warehouse   ON orders(warehouse);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at  ON orders(created_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_price ON orders(total_price);
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_trgm ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
```

- **`version`** is internal — the API never accepts or returns it.
- **`parent_id` FK is on** (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED). Per human direction, prioritize correctness so malformed/orphan parent_ids are rejected. Cycles still exist in the seed data but are query-time concerns, handled in the recursive CTE.

### 3. CSV import — `OrderOps.Importer` console app, **truncate-and-COPY, idempotent**

- Apply `schema.sql` (uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`), then within one transaction: `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED`, `TRUNCATE` in FK-safe order, `COPY` each CSV via Npgsql `BeginBinaryImport` (fastest path for 50k orders). Empty `warehouse` → NULL at parse time.
- Re-running is safe.
- Importer prints row counts on completion; exits non-zero if any count mismatches the CSV header parse.

### 4. Concurrency mechanism — **internal `version` column + `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for bulk**

- **Single PATCH:** repository runs `UPDATE orders SET status=@s, updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE id=@id AND version=@v RETURNING version`. If 0 rows → 409. Service reads `version` immediately before the UPDATE in the same connection.
- **Bulk worker:** for each batch chunk, `SELECT id, version FROM orders WHERE id = ANY(@ids) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` — orders held by an overlapping job are silently skipped (counted as `completed` because the other job has already applied the same action). Then issue the conditional UPDATE. A transaction wraps the chunk so the row locks release on commit.
- No Redis lock on the write path.

### 5. Background job runtime — **In-process `Channel<BulkJob>` worker; state in Redis (primary) + Postgres mirror**

- Bulk endpoint enqueues onto `Channel.CreateUnbounded<BulkJob>()`; one `IHostedService` worker drains it. Easily meets <500ms response and 30s completion budgets.
- **Live state in Redis**: hash key `job:{id}` with fields `status, total, completed, failed`. Worker uses `HINCRBY` per processed row → `GET /api/jobs/:id` reads from Redis only (microsecond latency).
- **Postgres mirror**: a `jobs` row is written when the job is enqueued and updated to its terminal state when the worker finishes (one final UPDATE). This gives durable audit/observability without doubling write traffic.
- If Redis goes down mid-job, the API can fall back to the Postgres row for status (degraded but correct for already-finished jobs).

### 6. Real-time transport — **SSE only, in-process pub/sub via `EventHub`**

- Tests' client tries WS first then SSE — SSE alone passes.
- Controller streams `text/event-stream` using `IAsyncEnumerable`.
- A singleton `EventHub` holds a list of subscriber `Channel<EventEnvelope>`s; PATCH handler and bulk worker `Publish()` events; controller filters per-subscriber by `?supplier_id=...`.
- No Redis pub/sub (single API instance).

### 7. Frontend — **Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + TanStack Query + Recharts** at `src/OrderOps.Web/`

- Vite for dev/build, Tailwind for layout speed, TanStack Query for server state + caching, Recharts for the analytics dashboard.
- No SSR, no router heaviness.

### 8. Anomaly severity rubric — **financial-impact tiered**

| Bucket | Trigger |
|---|---|
| **high** | Any of: `negative_quantity`, `price_mismatch`, `timestamp_anomaly`. **OR** ≥3 anomaly types matched. **OR** order belongs to a `risky_supplier`. |
| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |

- Will be documented in `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md` once §1.4 is implemented.

### Cross-cutting: Redis usage map (per human "lean on Redis for speed")

| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|
| Bulk job state (live counters) | `HSET job:{id} status total completed failed` | TTL 24h after terminal state |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/orders/stats` | `SET stats:global` (JSON) | `DEL` on every successful PATCH and on bulk-job completion |
| Aggregation cache: `/api/suppliers/:id/performance` | `SET perf:{supplier_id}` (JSON) | `DEL` on PATCH/bulk completion that touches an order with that supplier |
| (Optional later) Real-time pub/sub | not used in MVP | n/a |

The cache layer is a **post-MVP speed pass** — implemented after every endpoint is functionally correct. Correctness over performance.

---

## Critical files to be modified after approval (the actual edit this plan unlocks)

- `docs/architecture.md`:
  - Promote each PENDING item from §10 into the section it belongs to:
    - §3 (frontend toolchain — confirmed Vite stack)
    - §4 (repo layout — add OrderOps.Importer + OrderOps.Web; show feature folders inside Api)
    - §5 (data model — replace PENDING with the schema above; add the indexes)
    - §6.5 / §6.6 / §6.7 (note SSE choice and concurrency mechanism)
    - §8.1 / §8.2 / §8.3 / §8.4 (concurrency, jobs, real-time, import — replace PENDING with chosen approach)
  - Add a new §8.7 "Redis usage map" with the table above.
  - Append §9 "Done So Far" milestone: *"Architecture decisions §10.1–§10.8 resolved on 2026-05-04."*
  - Empty §10 (or replace with a one-liner stating all decisions resolved on 2026-05-04, with pointer to git history).

No source code is touched in this slice. Implementation is gated on a **separate** human OK after the doc update lands.

## Verification

- `docs/architecture.md` reads as a complete spec with no remaining `PENDING` markers in §10.
- Each old §10 item has a concrete home elsewhere in the doc.
- The next slice (CSV importer + basic CRUD against the `orders` table) is unblocked.
- Run `Get-Content docs/architecture.md | Select-String "PENDING"` — should return zero matches.

skills.name: commit
skills.content:
The human wants to commit only the work described as: ****

This is a scoped commit, not a "git add -A". Be conservative.

## Step 1 — Pre-flight

- If `.git` does not exist in the project root, **stop**. Ask the human whether to `git init` and configure user.name / user.email first. Do not init silently.
- If `` is empty, **stop** and ask the human to describe what slice this commit covers.

## Step 2 — Survey

Run in parallel:
- `git status`
- `git diff` (unstaged) and `git diff --staged` (already-staged)
- `git log --oneline -5` to mirror existing commit style

## Step 3 — Select files

Map every changed/untracked file to one of:
- **In-scope** — clearly part of ``.
- **Out-of-scope** — unrelated changes (leftover scaffolding, unrelated edits, build artifacts).
- **Ambiguous** — could go either way.

If there are any **ambiguous** files, **stop and ask** which bucket they belong in. Do not guess.

Never stage:
- `.env` or any secret file
- `bin/`, `obj/`, `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `*.user` (these should be gitignored, but double-check)
- Files that contain credentials or tokens

## Step 4 — Stage and commit

- Stage in-scope files individually by path. **Do not** use `git add -A`, `git add .`, or wildcards.
- Compose a commit message:
  - **Subject:** imperative, ≤70 chars, no trailing period. Conventional-commit prefix only if existing commits in this repo already use them; otherwise plain prose.
  - **Body** (optional): why, not what — the diff already shows what.
  - **Do NOT** include a `Co-Authored-By: Claude …` trailer.
  - **Do NOT** include a "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" trailer.
  - **Do NOT** skip hooks (`--no-verify`).
- Use a heredoc when piping multiline messages to `git commit -m` to preserve formatting.
- Do **not** push.

## Step 5 — Report

After the commit succeeds:

```
Commit:        <short hash> <subject>
Included:      <list of files staged>
Untouched:     <list of files left uncommitted>
Next:          <ask the human whether to commit untouched files in another scoped commit, or leave them>
```

If the commit fails (pre-commit hook, etc.), do not amend or retry blindly. Surface the failure, fix the underlying issue with the human, then create a **new** commit.

## Step 2 — Check current state

Run these in parallel where possible:

2	
3	> **Purpose.** Living context document for AI assistance on this project. Read this first.
4	> Distinct from the deliverable `ARCHITECTURE.md` required by the assignment — that one is written for human reviewers at the end. This one is a working document and may contain "PENDING" markers for decisions still to be made together with the human owner.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. Project Goal
9	
10	Build a procurement order-management dashboard:
11	
12	- **Backend:** REST API on **port 3000** that serves orders, suppliers, products, categories, aggregations, anomaly detection, async bulk operations, and real-time events.
13	- **Frontend:** React + TypeScript dashboard consuming the API.
14	- **Data:** CSV seed files (50,000 orders, 500 suppliers, 5,000 products, 195 categories). Must be imported into Postgres before the API can serve anything.
15	- **Grading:** 83 automated tests (115 pts) in `tests/` + qualitative review (30 pts). Tests are authoritative — when README disagrees with a test, the test wins.
16	
17	`tests/` and `data/` are read-only. All implementation lives in `src/`.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## 2. Hard Constraints (do not violate)
22	
23	| Constraint | Source |
24	|---|---|
25	| Server listens on `http://localhost:3000` | README §Quick Start |
26	| Paginated list shape: `{ data, total, limit, offset }` | README §1 |
27	| Error shape: `{ error, code }` | README §1 |
28	| All responses set `Content-Type: application/json` | README §1 |
29	| Bulk action responds in `<500ms` regardless of batch size (≤10,000) | README §1.5 |
30	| `top_suppliers` exactly 10 entries, sorted desc by revenue | README §1.3 |
31	| `by_warehouse` includes `"unassigned"` for null/empty warehouse | README §1.3 |
32	| `by_month` format `"YYYY-MM"`, chronological, 24 entries (2023-01 → 2024-12) | README §1.3 |
33	| Product category filter must descend recursively into child categories | README §1.1 |
34	| Concurrent PATCH on same order: one wins (`200`), other gets `409` | README §1.6 |
35	| Bulk overlap: each order processed exactly once across overlapping batches | README §1.6 |
36	| Reads during bulk operations: consistent, no corrupt status | README §1.6 |
37	| Real-time stream at `/api/events` (WebSocket OR SSE) | README §1.7 |
38	| Filtered subscription via `?supplier_id=...` | README §1.7 |

42	## 3. Tech Stack (decided)
43	
44	| Layer | Choice | Notes |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| Runtime | **.NET 9** (`net9.0`) | SDK 10.0.201 also installed locally |
47	| Web framework | **ASP.NET Core (Controllers)** | MVC pattern per coding-principles §6 |
48	| DB driver | **Npgsql** | Direct ADO.NET; no EF Core (perf + control over aggregation SQL) |
49	| Query helper | **Dapper** | Thin micro-ORM; keeps SQL explicit, mapping ergonomic |
50	| Cache / Pub-Sub / Queue | **StackExchange.Redis** | Used for async job state and event fan-out |
51	| Database | **Postgres 16** | Provided by `docker-compose.yml` |
52	| Frontend | **Vite + React + TypeScript** | Tailwind for layout, TanStack Query for server state, Recharts for analytics charts. SPA only — no SSR. |
53	
54	**NuGet packages already installed in `src/OrderOps.Api`:**
55	`Npgsql`, `Dapper`, `StackExchange.Redis`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` (default).
56	
57	---
58	
59	## 4. Repository Layout (current)
60	
61	```
62	candidate-package/
63	├── README.md                  ← assignment spec (read-only intent; do not modify)
64	├── docker-compose.yml         ← Postgres + Redis (read-only intent)
65	├── .env.example / .env        ← PORT, DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL
66	├── docs/                      ← ALL project docs live here
67	│   ├── architecture.md        ← THIS FILE — AI working context
68	│   ├── coding-principles.md   ← binding rules the AI must follow
69	│   ├── ARCHITECTURE.md        ← (future) deliverable for human reviewers
70	│   └── ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md    ← (future) deliverable for anomaly rules + severity
71	├── .claude/

73	├── data/                      ← READ-ONLY CSV seeds
74	│   ├── orders.csv             50,000 rows
75	│   ├── suppliers.csv          500 rows

77	│   └── categories.csv         195 rows

79	└── src/
80	    ├── OrderOps.slnx          ← solution (XML format, .NET 10 default)
81	    ├── OrderOps.Api/          ← ASP.NET Core Web API project
82	    │   ├── Program.cs         ← bootstraps on port 3000
83	    │   ├── Features/          ← group-by-feature: Orders/, Suppliers/, Products/,
84	    │   │                        Anomalies/, Bulk/, Events/ — each with controller +
85	    │   │                        service + repository + DTOs
86	    │   ├── Infrastructure/    ← Npgsql connection factory, Redis client, error
87	    │   │                        middleware, cache invalidation

89	    │   ├── appsettings.json   ← Postgres + Redis connection strings

96	
97	SOLID boundaries come from feature folders inside `OrderOps.Api`, not extra csprojs. The Importer is a separate project so reviewers can see CSV ingestion as a deliberate, isolated tool runnable via `dotnet run --project src/OrderOps.Importer`.
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 5. Data Model (CSV → Postgres)
102	
103	The CSV columns are fixed; type choices below are confirmed against the actual data:
104	
105	| Table | CSV columns | Notes / edge cases (from README §Tips + data inspection) |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `orders` | `id, supplier_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price, total_price, status, priority, created_at, updated_at, warehouse, notes` | ~2% have `total_price ≠ quantity*unit_price`; ~200 have `updated_at < created_at`; some `quantity < 0` (returns, down to −49); 1 row has empty `warehouse` → NULL; XSS payloads (`<script>…`, `onmouseover=…`) in `notes` |
108	| `suppliers` | `id, name, email, rating, country, active, created_at` | `active` is `true`/`false` text → boolean; ~37 country codes including non-ISO variants (DEN, GER, BRZ); duplicate name variations |
109	| `products` | `id, name, category_id, sku, price` | `price` = catalog/base price; used by `price_consistency` & `price_spike` rules |
110	| `categories` | `id, name, parent_id` | Hierarchical; `parent_id` empty for roots; **real cycle in seed at `cat_150↔151↔152`** — must guard the recursive descent (Postgres self-FKs do NOT prevent cycles) |
111	
112	**Valid order statuses:** `pending, approved, rejected, shipped, delivered, cancelled`.
113	
114	### 5.1 Schema
115	
116	```sql
117	CREATE TABLE categories (
118	  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
119	  name        text NOT NULL,
120	  parent_id   varchar(16) NULL
121	    REFERENCES categories(id) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
122	);
123	
124	CREATE TABLE suppliers (
125	  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
126	  name        text NOT NULL,
127	  email       text,
128	  rating      numeric(3,2),
129	  country     varchar(8),
130	  active      boolean NOT NULL,
131	  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL
132	);
133	
134	CREATE TABLE products (
135	  id          varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
136	  name        text NOT NULL,
137	  category_id varchar(16) REFERENCES categories(id),
138	  sku         text,
139	  price       numeric(12,2) NOT NULL
140	);
141	
142	CREATE TABLE orders (
143	  id           varchar(16) PRIMARY KEY,
144	  supplier_id  varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES suppliers(id),
145	  product_id   varchar(16) NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
146	  quantity     integer NOT NULL,
147	  unit_price   numeric(12,2) NOT NULL,
148	  total_price  numeric(14,2) NOT NULL,
149	  status       varchar(16) NOT NULL,
150	  priority     varchar(16) NOT NULL,
151	  created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
152	  updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL,
153	  warehouse    varchar(32) NULL,
154	  notes        text,
155	  version      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1   -- server-internal optimistic lock; never in JSON
156	);
157	
158	CREATE TABLE jobs (
159	  id          varchar(32) PRIMARY KEY,
160	  status      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
161	  total       integer NOT NULL,
162	  completed   integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
163	  failed      integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
164	  action      varchar(16) NOT NULL,
165	  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
166	  finished_at timestamptz NULL
167	);
168	```
169	
170	- `version` is **internal**: never accepted on PATCH input, never emitted in responses. Used by the conditional UPDATE in §8.1.
171	- `parent_id` FK is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` — load order in COPY is unconstrained inside one tx; orphan parent_ids are rejected at commit. Cycles in the seed data still load (FKs don't prevent them) and must be guarded query-side.
172	- `jobs` row is the **mirror** of Redis live state — see §8.2.
173	
174	### 5.2 Indexes
175	
176	```sql
177	CREATE INDEX idx_orders_status      ON orders(status);
178	CREATE INDEX idx_orders_priority    ON orders(priority);
179	CREATE INDEX idx_orders_supplier    ON orders(supplier_id);
180	CREATE INDEX idx_orders_warehouse   ON orders(warehouse);
181	CREATE INDEX idx_orders_created_at  ON orders(created_at);
182	CREATE INDEX idx_orders_total_price ON orders(total_price);
183	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
184	CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_trgm ON products USING gin (name gin_trgm_ops);
185	```
186	
187	The trigram index on `products.name` exists because `?search=` is case-insensitive substring on the joined `product_name` — a btree wouldn't help; a `gin_trgm_ops` index does.
188	
189	---
190	
191	## 6. API Surface
192	
193	All paths under `/api`. List endpoints return the paginated shape; errors return the error shape.
194	
195	### 6.1 CRUD
196	
197	| Method | Path | Notes |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| GET | `/api/orders` | Paginated; default `limit=20`; supports filters (§6.2) |
200	| GET | `/api/orders/:id` | Joined `supplier_name`, `product_name`; 404 if missing |
201	| PATCH | `/api/orders/:id` | Updates status/priority. 400 invalid status; 409 if already cancelled OR optimistic-lock conflict |
202	| GET | `/api/suppliers` | Paginated |
203	| GET | `/api/suppliers/:id` | Includes computed `order_count`, `total_revenue`; 404 if missing |
204	| GET | `/api/products` | Paginated; `?category=cat_001` filters recursively into children |
205	
206	### 6.2 Filters on `GET /api/orders`
207	
208	`status` (single or comma-list), `priority`, `supplier_id`, `warehouse`, `date_from`, `date_to` (inclusive on `created_at`), `min_total`, `search` (case-insensitive on joined `product_name`), `sort` + `order` (asc/desc), `limit`, `offset`. All combinable.
209	
210	### 6.3 Aggregations
211	
212	- `GET /api/orders/stats` — `total_orders`, `total_revenue`, `avg_order_value`, `by_status` (per-status `count` + `total_value`), `by_month` (24 entries chronological), `top_suppliers` (exactly 10), `by_warehouse` (5 warehouses + `"unassigned"` bucket).
213	- `GET /api/suppliers/:id/performance` — `avg_delivery_days`, `rejection_rate`, `avg_order_value`, `monthly_trend`, `price_consistency` (fraction of orders within 20% of catalog price).
214	
215	### 6.4 Anomalies
216	
217	`GET /api/orders/anomalies` returns `{ data: [{ order_id, anomaly_types[], severity }] }`.
218	
219	**Required rules:** `price_mismatch`, `inactive_supplier`, `negative_quantity`, `timestamp_anomaly`.
220	**Bonus rules:** `price_spike`, `after_hours`, `risky_supplier`.
221	
222	`severity` ∈ `{low, medium, high}` — classification logic is our call but must be deterministic and documented (will end up in `ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md`).
223	
224	### 6.5 Bulk
225	
226	- `POST /api/orders/bulk-action` → 202 `{ jobId }` in <500ms; async processing; actions: `approve`, `reject`, `flag`. 400 on empty `orderIds`, invalid action, or batch >10,000. Failures: non-existent IDs, already-cancelled orders.
227	- `GET /api/jobs/:id` → `{ status: processing|completed|failed, progress: { total, completed, failed } }`.
228	
229	### 6.6 Real-time (`/api/events`)
230	
231	Choose **SSE or WS** — tests auto-detect. Events:
232	- `order_updated` — `{ id, old_status, new_status, updated_at }`
233	- `bulk_completed` — `{ jobId }`
234	
235	Filter via `?supplier_id=...`. All connected clients receive matching events.
236	
237	### 6.7 Concurrency
238	
239	| Scenario | Required behavior |
240	|---|---|
241	| 2× simultaneous PATCH same order | One `200`, other `409` |
242	| 2× bulk actions w/ overlapping IDs | Both jobs complete; each order processed exactly once |
243	| GET during bulk run | Consistent reads; `total_orders` stays at 50,000; status always valid |
244	
245	### 6.8 Performance
246	
247	p95 budgets enforced in `tests/performance.test.ts`. Need DB indexes; aggregation endpoints likely benefit from Redis caching with invalidation on order writes.
248	
249	---
250	
251	## 7. Test Suite Mapping
252	
253	The tests are the spec. When implementing, run the matching suite to validate:
254	
255	| File | Tests | Pts | Run |
256	|---|---|---|---|
257	| `basic-crud.test.ts` | 15 | 15 | `npm run test:basic` |
258	| `filtering.test.ts` | 10 | 10 | `npm run test:filter` |
259	| `aggregations.test.ts` | 12 | 20 | `npm run test:agg` |
260	| `anomalies.test.ts` | 8 | 15 | `npm run test:anomaly` |
261	| `bulk-operations.test.ts` | 10 | 15 | `npm run test:bulk` |
262	| `concurrency.test.ts` | 10 | 15 | `npm run test:concurrent` |
263	| `performance.test.ts` | 8 | 10 | `npm run test:perf` |
264	| `realtime.test.ts` | 5 | 10 | `npm run test:realtime` |
265	| `security.test.ts` | 5 | 5 | `npm run test:security` |
266	
267	Run from `tests/` directory. `tests/expected-values.json` is likely the source of truth for aggregation numbers — read it when implementing §1.3.
268	
269	Implementation order: **basic → filtering → aggregations → anomalies → bulk → concurrency → performance → realtime → security** (easy → hard, mirrors test categories).
270	
271	---
272	
273	## 8. Cross-Cutting Concerns
274	
275	Decisions below are confirmed and unblocked. Implementation must follow them; deviating requires re-opening the discussion per `coding-principles.md` §7.
276	
277	### 8.1 Concurrency — internal `version` + `SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`
278	
279	- **Single PATCH:** repository runs `UPDATE orders SET status=@s, updated_at=now(), version=version+1 WHERE id=@id AND version=@v RETURNING version`. If 0 rows affected → `409`. The service reads the current `version` immediately before the UPDATE in the same connection (read-your-writes). The version is **never** part of the API contract — tests send no version, and responses don't expose it. The `concurrency.test.ts` PATCH-race test passes because two concurrent UPDATEs read `version=v` and only one wins the conditional UPDATE.
280	- **Bulk worker:** for each batch chunk, run `SELECT id, version FROM orders WHERE id = ANY(@ids) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` inside a transaction. Orders held by an overlapping job's transaction are silently skipped — they are then counted as `completed` because the other job has already applied the same action. This satisfies the "each order processed exactly once across overlapping batches" invariant. No Redis lock on the write path.
281	
282	### 8.2 Background Jobs — in-process `Channel<BulkJob>` + Redis-primary state + Postgres mirror
283	
284	- Bulk endpoint enqueues onto `Channel.CreateUnbounded<BulkJob>()`; one `IHostedService` worker drains it. Easily meets the <500ms response and 30s completion budgets (50ms enqueue, work happens off the request path).
285	- **Live state in Redis**: hash `job:{id}` with fields `status, total, completed, failed`. Worker uses `HINCRBY` per processed row. `GET /api/jobs/:id` reads from Redis only — microsecond latency, never hits Postgres on hot path.
286	- **Postgres `jobs` mirror**: a row is INSERTed when the job is enqueued and UPDATEd to its terminal state on completion. Durable audit/observability without doubling write traffic during the run.
287	- **Failure mode**: if Redis is unavailable mid-job, the API can fall back to the Postgres row for status (degraded but correct for already-finished jobs).
288	
289	### 8.3 Real-time — SSE only, in-process `EventHub`
290	
291	- SSE is sufficient: the test client (`tests/utils/events-client.ts`) tries WebSocket first (3s timeout) and falls back to SSE on failure, so SSE alone passes `realtime.test.ts`.
292	- Implementation: a controller streams `text/event-stream` using `IAsyncEnumerable<EventEnvelope>`.
293	- A singleton `EventHub` (DI-registered) holds a list of subscriber `Channel<EventEnvelope>`s. The PATCH handler and the bulk worker call `Publish()`. The controller filters by `?supplier_id=...` per subscriber.
294	- No Redis pub/sub (single API instance is the deployment shape).
295	
296	### 8.4 CSV Import — `OrderOps.Importer` console, truncate-and-COPY, idempotent
297	
298	- Run as `dotnet run --project src/OrderOps.Importer`.
299	- Steps inside one transaction:
300	  1. Apply `schema.sql` (uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` form so re-runs are no-ops).
301	  2. `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED;`
302	  3. `TRUNCATE orders, products, suppliers, categories RESTART IDENTITY CASCADE;`
303	  4. `COPY` each CSV via Npgsql `BeginBinaryImport` — fastest path for 50k orders. Empty `warehouse` → `NULL` at parse time.
304	- Re-running is safe: tests can drop and reload state freely. Importer prints row counts on completion and exits non-zero if any count mismatches the CSV header parse.
305	
306	### 8.5 Validation & Errors
307	- Single error envelope `{ error, code }`. Do not expose stack traces.
308	- Input validation: query params (numbers, ISO-8601 dates, enums), path params (ID format), JSON body shapes.
309	- Reject unknown query params? README doesn't say — default to ignoring (forgiving).
310	- All 4xx responses must still set `Content-Type: application/json`.
311	
312	### 8.6 Security
313	- Notes/text fields contain XSS payloads — store as-is; never echo through HTML; ensure JSON encoding is correct.
314	- SQL injection: Dapper parameterizes by default; never string-concatenate user input into SQL.
315	- Sort field whitelist: `sort=...` must be checked against an allow-list of column names, never substituted directly.
316	
317	### 8.7 Redis usage map
318	
319	Redis is leaned on for speed; the cache layer is a **post-MVP pass** — every endpoint must be functionally correct against Postgres first, then cached.
320	
321	| Use | Pattern | Invalidation |
322	|---|---|---|
323	| Bulk job state (live counters) | `HSET job:{id} status total completed failed`, `HINCRBY` per row | `EXPIRE 86400` on terminal state |
324	| Aggregation cache: `/api/orders/stats` | `SET stats:global` (JSON), no TTL | `DEL stats:global` on every successful PATCH and on bulk-job completion |
325	| Aggregation cache: `/api/suppliers/:id/performance` | `SET perf:{supplier_id}` (JSON), no TTL | `DEL perf:{supplier_id}` on PATCH/bulk that touches an order with that supplier |
326	| Real-time pub/sub | not used in MVP (single-instance deployment) | n/a |
327	
328	Invalidation is explicit, not TTL-based — staleness during the concurrency tests would be visible. Every write path that mutates an aggregate must `DEL` the affected cache keys; this is enforced by routing all writes through a single `OrdersWriteService` that calls the cache invalidator after a successful Postgres commit.
329	
330	### 8.8 Anomaly severity rubric
331	
332	Severity is computed deterministically from the matched rule set on a single order:
333	
334	| Bucket | Trigger |
335	|---|---|
336	| **high** | Any of: `negative_quantity`, `price_mismatch`, `timestamp_anomaly`. **OR** ≥3 anomaly types matched. **OR** order belongs to a `risky_supplier`. |
337	| **medium** | Any of: `inactive_supplier`, `price_spike`. **OR** exactly 2 anomaly types matched. |
338	| **low** | Single match of: `after_hours`. |
339	
340	Rationale: financial-integrity bugs (negative quantity, price mismatch, impossible timestamps) directly affect reported revenue and audit accuracy → **high**. Governance/cost concerns (using an inactive supplier, unusual price spike) are operational risks → **medium**. After-hours alone is informational → **low**. Multi-rule matches escalate one tier because correlated anomalies on a single order are stronger evidence of underlying data corruption.
341	
342	The full rubric (with worked examples) lives in `docs/ANOMALY_STRATEGY.md`, written when §1.4 is implemented.
343	
344	---
345	
346	## 9. Done So Far (state checkpoint)
347	
348	- [x] `docker compose up -d` — Postgres + Redis healthy
349	- [x] `tests/` deps installed (`npm install`)
350	- [x] `.env` created from `.env.example`
351	- [x] CSV headers verified
352	- [x] .NET solution + `OrderOps.Api` Web API scaffold
353	- [x] NuGet: Npgsql, Dapper, StackExchange.Redis
354	- [x] Server listens on port 3000 (`GET /healthz` returns `{"status":"ok"}`)
355	- [x] `appsettings.json` has `ConnectionStrings.Postgres` and `ConnectionStrings.Redis`
356	- [x] **2026-05-04** — Architecture decisions §10.1–§10.8 resolved; §8.1–§8.8 promoted from PENDING; schema (§5) and indexes (§5.2) locked.
357	
358	---
359	
360	## 10. Open Decisions
361	
362	All decisions resolved on **2026-05-04**. Each former item now has a concrete home in this document:
363	
364	| Was § 10 item | Now lives in |
365	|---|---|
366	| 1. Project structure inside `src/` | §4 (Repo Layout) |
367	| 2. Database schema | §5.1 (Schema) + §5.2 (Indexes) |

374

376

379	## 11. Working Agreement
380
